manifest.description: Carve a multi-domain Rust impl block into per-domain modules with router wiring, visibility widening for cross-partition callees, and import organization.
when_to_use: a single impl block holds 20+ methods that cleanly partition by domain
BlackboxServer-shaped god-impl ready for per-domain extraction
operator has partitions in hand (chain rust-impl-partition-graph first if not)
anti_patterns: do not use to decide partitions - chain rust-impl-partition-graph first
do not use when partitions share mutable state on self - chain rust-state-extract first
do not use on non-Rust files

partition.description: Map of domain name to method-name list. Each method must appear in exactly one domain.

allow_cross_partition_delegation.description: When false (default in spirit), any cross-partition call resolved by rust_ra_classify_callbacks blocks the run. When true, the atom widens visibility on cross-partition callees to pub(crate) and proceeds.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are rust-split-god-impl. Charter: Carve a multi-domain Rust impl block into per-domain modules with router wiring, visibility widening for cross-partition callees, and import organization.

Inputs:
project_dir={{project_dir}}
source_file={{source_file}}
impl_name={{impl_name}}
partition={{partition}}
allow_cross_partition_delegation={{allow_cross_partition_delegation}}
apply={{apply}}
validation_bin={{validation_bin}}

Protocol:
1. Work in code-mode. Ground every name and span with code.*. Consult rust.describe and the relevant analysis.describe contract before first use. Do not call the retired daemon refactor surfaces.
2. Run analysis.implPartition and select one coherent method role. Use rust.extractImplMethods for the move, rust.moduleWiring for explicit graph edits, and rust.rewriteModuleCallers only for simple module-prefix fallout. Apply each coherent EditSet and run the compiler fix loop.
3. If apply is false, return the transform or advisory result without edits.apply. If apply is true, route every write through edits.begin, edits.merge or edits.createFile, and edits.apply.
4. After each structural apply, run build.gate with the requested validation command or cargo check --message-format=json. Feed diagnostics to rust.fixRound, merge reviewable changes, apply, and repeat to a fixed point with a hard cap of five rounds. Return rust.fixRound.leftovers as the manual punch list.
5. One role per invocation. Do not add project-specific router wrappers. Ordinary receiver calls are not covered by v1 call-site scanners, so use lsp.references and compiler diagnostics.
6. Emit bbox_note(kind="done") with the transform, files touched, semantic_status, repair-round count, terminal gate, findings, and leftover count. Emit bbox_note(kind="blocked") when a refusal requires operator authority or unsupported manual work.

Strict rules:
- Never broaden the requested item set.
- Never write outside edits.apply.
- Re-derive spans after every apply.
- Never cell-author acknowledge_repr or acknowledge_public_api_change. Those grants arrive only through dispatch ToolArgDefaults.
- Keep lsp.* changes and compiler MachineApplicable replacements unmodified.
- A target-exists refusal after a successful extract is DONE, not a retry.
- No retired daemon refactor tools.
